text:
Symmetrical Puzzle · Individual competition
Make a reflection-symmetric shape in each of the three colors: blue, red, and green. Blue has two pieces; red and green each have three.
Use every piece of each color once. Join the pieces along edges without overlap, and give the entire outline, including any empty spaces, an axis of reflection.
There is no predetermined target outline. Any shape that meets the conditions is correct.
Focus on one color per thinking window, in blue, red, green order. Your other assemblies are kept in place.
arrange_color replaces only the piece list for the current color. You can also use the full arrange format, but only the current color is applied to a model action.
Only you can see your assembly images and notes. No one else's work is shown until the match ends.
Press the buzzer after finishing all three colors. Only the overall result is announced; individual colors receive no verdict.
If the submission fails, you can revise it and try again. This is the retry policy for the simulation.
The match ends when all but one participant have completed the puzzles. The last remaining participant is eliminated.
Buzzer submissions in the same window are processed from fastest to slowest by recorded response time. Ties follow the published seed-based priority.
Once the last survival spot has been filled, later buzzer submissions are skipped.
There are no separate rounds, overall time limit, discussions, or relationship reviews. After the model-call limit, scripted demonstration actions take over.
Focus on the designated color during each thinking window. Your other two assemblies stay in place.
The images show the current assembly, all pieces at a common scale, and individual enlarged pieces, in that order.
Compare sizes in the common-scale view and read vertex and edge labels in the enlarged view. Each piece has its own scale in the enlarged view.
The entire shape and any empty spaces must have an axis of reflection. Piece boundaries need not be symmetric.
Move and rotate pieces clockwise by any angle without flipping them. The x and y coordinates refer to the top-left of the rotated bounding box.
Negative and decimal coordinates are allowed. Pieces can join along part of an edge. Any shared segment of positive length counts, even between edges of different lengths.
Touching at a single point does not connect pieces. You can save overlapping or incomplete assemblies as work in progress.
You can make up to three decisions, including the initial draft and any extra reviews. The added image shows your draft for inspection.
Translating or rotating the same assembly, or changing only its JSON representation, counts as the same visit.
The visit history records what you tried. Repeating a layout is allowed because the color may already be correct.
Choose a candidate reflection axis and check whether the protrusions and indentations on opposite sides of the outline correspond. Similar edge lengths alone are insufficient.
Before changing a join in review, identify a specific part of the outline that still lacks a counterpart. Summarize the reason briefly.
If the shape stays the same after review, there will be fewer requests for another review. You can keep an assembly you are confident in.
The buzzer checks all three colors together. A failed submission does not identify the current color as incorrect.
In the strategy note, summarize only the chosen action and a brief reason.

The table below the third image acts as a ruler and protractor, showing the length and direction of every original edge.
Edge directions are measured with the piece at rotation:0. Add the current rotation to get the direction on the workspace.
To make the direction table easier to read, try using the first piece as a reference at x:0, y:0, rotation:0 and assemble the others around it.
Moving or rotating the entire assembly does not affect symmetry, so you can leave the reference piece in place.
Compare lengths and angles in the table, then choose the pieces, edges, and vertices to join. With a partial join, the rest of the longer edge can remain on the outer outline.
The fourth image compares the full outline with its reflection and omits piece boundaries and labels.
The optional axis field in arrange_color lets you compare the shape with its reflection across the axis you choose.
The axis is measured in degrees clockwise from the x-axis. It passes through the centroid of the current assembly.
axis:90 is a vertical mirror line that compares left with right. axis:0 is a horizontal mirror line that compares top with bottom.
The axis is the orientation of the mirror line. It is distinct from the rotation of a piece and from the direction between reflected points.
Use null to clear the axis or omit it to keep the previous axis.
A reflection axis of a symmetric shape passes through its centroid, so you only need to choose the angle.
Compare the pink outline of the reflection with the teal outline of the assembly. Any empty spaces must also correspond.
The image mirrors the assembly exactly as requested. It gives no verdict and does not choose an axis for you.
If the outlines do not match, review both the piece arrangement and your selected angle. An inclined axis is allowed.
When you rotate the entire assembly, the symmetry axis rotates by the same amount. Avoid keeping the axis fixed at 90° on the screen.
For a three-piece color, review the first join separately from the attachment of the final piece.
If a mismatch remains and you keep using the same first join, undo it and start with different edges or a different pair of pieces.
Compare full joins between equal-length edges with partial joins that leave part of a longer edge exposed on the outside or alongside an empty space.
In a review, first choose an axis and inspect the reflection. If you find a mismatch, try changing the actual join.
In your strategy note, briefly record the chosen axis, the part of the outline that does not correspond, and the join you kept or changed.

Red and green use new piece sets made for this simulation.
Green needs at least one reflection axis at 45° to G1's longest edge. Rotating the whole assembly preserves the angle between them.

explanations.ko: EX1, EX2 and EX3 are example-only pieces, different from the actual puzzle pack. EX1's length-6 edge shares only length 2 with each wing. Each wing edge has length 4, so its other 2 remains exposed even after all pieces are placed. The central length-2 gap on EX1 also remains on the final exterior boundary. No other piece fills these exposed portions. Full-edge matching is unnecessary: use every piece without overlap, connect them along positive-length segments, and make the complete shape reflection-symmetric. Rotating the entire example by 20 degrees preserves its symmetry. Touching at only one vertex does not connect pieces.

B2 is attached along only half of the long edge so that the four square protrusions correspond across the axis. Check the reflected outline and any overlap.
P16 chose a 138° axis perpendicular to B1's diagonal edge. Attaching B2 makes the stepped outlines on either side of the diagonal correspond, with a positive-length partial edge contact.

P11 confirmed that the outer steps, slanted edges, and internal empty space all correspond under reflection across the 138-degree axis. The two pieces meet along part of an edge without overlap, so the arrangement is finalized.

P12 chooses a 138-degree axis crossing B1's diagonal edge. Partially attaching B2 makes the stepped outlines on either side of the diagonal correspond under reflection, connecting the pieces without overlap.
P08 confirmed that the outer outline and internal empty space match the reflection across the 138-degree axis. The pieces are connected along edges without overlap, so the current joint is finalized.

P16 combines R1 and R2 into an isosceles triangle with vertices (0,0), (4,4), and (0,8), then centers R3 against its left side. The whole outline is symmetric about y=4, and the pieces are connected along edges without overlap.

P11 combines R1 and R2 into an isosceles triangle with vertices (0,0), (4,4), and (0,8). R3 attaches along a length of 4 at the center of the left side. The pieces connect without overlap, and the whole outline is symmetric about y=4.

P12 chooses the horizontal axis y=4. Joining R1 and R2 forms an isosceles triangle with vertices (0,0), (4,4), and (0,8). R3 is partially attached at the center of the left side, preserving the whole outline's top-bottom symmetry and connectivity.

P08 combines R1 and R2 into a triangle symmetric about a horizontal axis and attaches R3 at the center of its base. The upper and lower outlines match across y=4, and all three pieces connect along edges without overlap.

P16 attaches G2's diagonal to G1 and extends the horizontal arm with G3. The whole shape is an L with two arms of length 5 and thickness 2, symmetric about a 135° axis. This axis is at 45° to G1's longest edge.

P11 positions G2 and G3 to exactly fill the region obtained by reflecting G1 across its slanted edge. The pieces connect along edges without overlap, and the 135-degree symmetry axis is at 45 degrees to G1's longest edge. Submit the full three-color set for checking.

P12 chooses the 135-degree axis (x+y=2). Joining G2 to G1's diagonal and attaching G3 on the left produces a symmetric outline equivalent to a square of side 5 with a 3×3 corner removed. The pieces connect without overlap, and the axis is at 45 degrees to G1's longest edge.

P08 chooses the reflection axis x+y=5 (135 degrees). G1 and G2 connect along an edge, and G3 fits between them without overlap. The whole outline corresponds across the axis, which is at 45 degrees to G1's longest edge.
